CASE.focal_event: NVIDIA cuts preliminary quarterly revenue estimate as gaming sales weaken

company.name: NVIDIA
company.profile: NVIDIA is a U.S. semiconductor and computing-platform company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designs GPUs and related systems and software for gaming, professional visualization, data centers and automotive applications. Its computing platforms combine processor hardware with software, libraries and developer tools, including CUDA for parallel computing. The company uses external manufacturers to fabricate, assemble and test its products rather than owning semiconductor wafer-fabrication plants. Its results depend on end-market demand, product mix and pricing, development and manufacturing costs, access to manufacturing capacity and the timely introduction and acceptance of new products. This general business description uses information available in its fiscal 2020 annual report; no later product launches, acquisitions, financial results or customer agreements are assumed unless included in the supplied article.

articles.title: NVIDIA cuts preliminary quarterly revenue estimate as gaming sales weaken
articles.text: NVIDIA estimated revenue of $6.70 billion for the quarter ended July 31, 2022, versus its previously issued $8.10 billion outlook. The preliminary figure was down 19% sequentially and up 3% year over year. Gaming revenue was $2.04 billion, down 44% sequentially and 33% year over year. Management attributed the shortfall primarily to lower Gaming sell-in and channel-partner demand amid macroeconomic headwinds. Data Center revenue of $3.81 billion rose 61% year over year but was below NVIDIA's expectations because of supply-chain disruption. NVIDIA expected approximately $1.32 billion of inventory and related charges. Preliminary GAAP gross margin was 43.7%, compared with the prior 65.1% outlook. Financial closing procedures were unfinished and estimates could change.
